concept.centerRule: A Scene belongs when the source gives a visible sacrificial act or explicitly applies sacrificial language. Similarity never erases differences in gift, recipient, place, purpose, or effect.

characterAnchors.label: Abel
characterAnchors.note: Brings firstborn animals and becomes the first person whose offering receives explicit divine regard.

characterAnchors.label: Noah
characterAnchors.note: Builds the first named altar after the flood.

characterAnchors.label: Abraham
characterAnchors.note: Builds altars, enters covenant, and is tested over Isaac.

characterAnchors.note: Mediates Passover, covenant blood, altar law, priestly instruction, and intercession.

characterAnchors.label: Aaron
characterAnchors.note: Serves as priest, offers for himself and Israel, and stands between living and dead.

characterAnchors.label: Saul
characterAnchors.note: Uses sacrifice inside two scenes of royal disobedience.

characterAnchors.label: David
characterAnchors.note: Brings the ark with sacrifice and later buys an altar site during plague.

characterAnchors.label: Elijah
characterAnchors.note: Repairs the altar at Carmel and asks which god will answer.

characterAnchors.label: Isaiah
characterAnchors.note: Rejects violent worship and presents the servant whose life becomes an offering.

characterAnchors.label: John the Baptist
characterAnchors.note: Points to Jesus as the Lamb of God.

characterAnchors.label: Jesus Christ
characterAnchors.note: Names covenant blood, lays down his life, dies at Passover, and is interpreted as priest and offering.

characterAnchors.label: Paul
characterAnchors.note: Uses sacrifice language for Christ, embodied worship, service, gifts, and table participation.

concept.throughline: The pattern moves from early gifts and altars through Israel’s differentiated offerings, priesthood, feasts, royal and prophetic conflict, Jesus’ death, apostolic interpretation, and Revelation’s Lamb and altar images.
